routes.description: Establish consciousness as the sole immediate ontological datum, reject nonconscious emergence as an explanation of experience, and show that a universal mental foundation can preserve objective structure, causal order, and scientific tractability.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if consciousness is shown to require no reduction to a nonexperiential substrate, while the proposed consciousness-first ontology accounts for observer-independent reality, differentiated subjects, regular causation, and nonspatiotemporal structure.

motionBridge.description: Connect the irreducibility of experience and the explanatory adequacy of universal subjectivity to the conclusion that consciousness is reality's ontological foundation.

centralBridges.description: Show why descriptions of nonconscious physical quantities cannot entail experiential qualities and why positing strong emergence does not close that explanatory gap.
Explain how an external mental reality can remain observer-independent and appear as a stable physical world through perceptual representation and dissociative boundaries.
Ground causal power, differentiation, and natural regularities in the intrinsic dispositions and excitation modes of universal subjectivity.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish the constructed narrative self from consciousness itself so that rejecting a persistent personal agent does not eliminate experience.
Account for structure beyond fundamental spacetime through meaning-bearing cognitive or semantic relations.

routes.description: Separate rejection of materialist emergence from acceptance of idealism, develop a representation-based neutral monism, and require any consciousness-first ontology to explain structured order, boundaries, causal differentiation, and phenomenal character.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if a neutral representational basis can accommodate phenomenal character without treating consciousness as universal substance, while idealism's mental-substrate designation leaves indispensable explanatory work unresolved.

motionBridge.description: Connect the sufficiency of neutral monism and the unresolved explanatory commitments of idealism to denial that consciousness must be reality's ontological foundation.

centralBridges.description: Establish that rejecting matter-to-consciousness emergence does not by itself select analytic idealism over other nonmaterialist ontologies.
Locate phenomenal character in representations without requiring a separate physical organism, unified self, or universal conscious substance.
Require an account of how a designated mental substrate produces boundaries, predictive representations, structured order, and differentiated causal relations.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test whether information integration supplies an explanatory connection to subjective experience rather than only an empirical correlation.
Use experiences lacking ordinary selfhood, space, or time to examine which features an adequate fundamental ontology must explain.

sections.title: Ontological Starting Point and the Emergence Gap
sections.rationale: This issue tests the principal inference from consciousness as an immediate datum and the explanatory gap of strong emergence to a consciousness-first ontology, including whether that inference excludes neutral alternatives.

sections.title: Objective Reality, Boundaries, and Natural Order
sections.rationale: A viable route must explain how observer-independent structure, perceptual representation, embodied boundaries, evolution, and stable causal regularities arise under its proposed ontology.

sections.title: Representation, Self-Models, and Phenomenal Character
sections.rationale: The dispute over whether phenomenal character belongs to representations, consciousness itself, or a persistent subject bears directly on whether neutral monism suffices or idealism is required.

sections.title: Integrated Information and Causal Existence
sections.rationale: This issue concerns whether information integration merely predicts reports or supports claims about subjective viewpoints, self-existing complexes, and the location of causal power.

sections.title: Universal Subjectivity, Differentiation, and Nonspatiotemporal Structure
sections.rationale: The proposed universal subject must account for differentiated experiences and causal order without relying on a personal self, while also explaining structure when ordinary space and time are not fundamental.
